Version using UNICODE block. Treats the name as just a string of characters and searches for capital letters in it. So if the name were "BeAuTy and jOy of computiNg" the block would report BATON.

Version using an additional SPLIT block. This version respects the abstraction that text is made up of words, not characters. It introduces hyphens as another word delimiter (in addition to spaces). It has an unfortunately hairy structure of higher order function calls. because the split by hyphens has to be done in each word separately (that's the inner MAP) and then the result has to be flattened (the APPEND). The ideal solution would split into words based on spaces and hyphens together, but Snap! doesn't have that capability (yet).
